gallery.title: File:Hull, Holy Trinity church window (29053166025).jpg
gallery.description:
Glass by Mary Hutchinson, 1920, commemorating the deliverance of Lille and the safe return of Rev. David Keys Moore. Given by James and Catherine Lofthouse, to whom Hutchison was related.

The design is based on the text "Therefore, with angels and archangels and with all the company of heaven we laud and magnify thy glorious name". The four large figures—from left to right—represent Gabriel, Michael, Uriel and Raphael.

gallery.title: File:Holy Trinity Church, Hull (geograph 234700).jpg
gallery.description: Holy Trinity Church, Kingston upon Hull,  East Riding of Yorkshire, England. Holy Trinity is said to be the largest by area of all English Parish Churches. The present building is the third Church on the site. Founded in 1285, the oldest parts date back to c1300. The 150 ft high tower (which contains four clock faces), has a ring of 15 bells.

gallery.title: File:A63 Feb23 Castle Street.jpg
gallery.description: A view of Castle Street, Kingston upon Hull, in February 2023, photographed from the 'Murdoch's Connection' footbridge. Temporary barriers have been erected while major roadworks are underway on the Mytongate roundabout. Hull Minster's tower and the city's Premier Inn are also visible in the background.
